changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For payments leaders, replace the average-uplift line with an account-specific one: 'Your approval rate in each market, by card type and issuer, and what we'd fix.' Say 'approvals', not 'authorization' or 'uplift'. Back it with an analysis of their own traffic, not the Authorization Boost average.
changes.why: We led with the average uplift. The buyer rejected it out loud ('that's an average. What's mine?') and said 'I can't take an average to my CFO'. He was asking about approvals by country, card type and issuer.

changes.change: For renewing accounts where a new payments leader has taken over, open with a per-market review of their own approvals and declines before they run one themselves. Frame it as 'money left on the table' in their markets, list the specific issues we would fix, and deliver it fast, before any competitor test finishes.
changes.why: The new head of payments started by pulling declines by country. Our analysis was called 'the most useful thing we'd sent him', but it landed three weeks after he asked, when the competitor's test had already finished.

changes.change: Add a proof point to the support story for payments leaders: a named person at Stripe who reviews their approvals every month, by market, and brings them what to fix. Keep this separate from the response-time tiers.
changes.why: The buyer asked who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month and the rep had no name. What he wanted was a market-by-market view of his own approval rates, with reasons.

changes.change: Instruction for marketing (no copy until the answer is confirmed): write a direct answer to 'why not local acquiring?' for international markets, and decide whether we can offer a test on the prospect's own international traffic with results reported by country.
changes.why: The competitor won by testing on the buyer's own traffic and reporting results by country, and the buyer had adopted the 'Local cards, local rails' frame. Our rep had no answer to 'local acquiring'.
